original_question: Let Omega be a smooth bounded planar domain and let T : L2 (Omega) 7→ L2 (Omega) be the Kohn solution operator for ∂/∂ z̄. For h ∈ L∞ (Omega) we define the compact non-self-adjoint operator Sh : L2 (Omega) 7→ L2 (Omega), f 7→ h̄T f . Under what circumstance will Sh have eigenvalues? Consider in particular the case where h is holomorphic. If h has a single-valued holomorphic primitive H then it is not hard to see that Sh has no eigenvalues. (Just note that e−H̄/λ T f is holomorphic and orthogonal to holomorphic functions.) Does the converse hold? That is: do periods of H guarantee the existence of eigenvalues? (For annuli, the answer is“yes.”) -D. Barrett, barrett@math.lsa.umich.edu
target_in_paper: Unnumbered Scratchpad problem contributed by D. Barrett concerning the compact operator S_h=\overline{h}\,T associated to the planar \bar\partial-solution operator, with emphasis on the holomorphic case and whether nontrivial periods of h(z)\,dz force nonzero eigenvalues.
correct_elements: The draft already captures the core setting and almost certainly the intended target very closely: a smooth bounded planar domain \Omega, the Kohn/canonical L^2 solution operator T for \partial/\partial\bar z, the compact operator S_hf=\overline{h}\,Tf, the special case of holomorphic h, the easy no-eigenvalue argument when h has a single-valued holomorphic primitive H, and the sharpened converse question asking whether nontrivial periods force eigenvalues; it also preserves the paper's annulus benchmark ('for annuli, yes').
missing_details: The operator T should be identified explicitly as the canonical L^2-minimal solution operator for \bar\partial on functions: for f\in L^2(\Omega), u=Tf is the unique solution of \bar\partial u=f orthogonal to the Bergman space A^2(\Omega).
The eigenvalue question should specify nonzero eigenvalues \lambda\in\mathbb C, since 0 can be a special case for compact operators and is not the spectral issue of interest here.
In the holomorphic case one should keep the boundedness hypothesis from the original setup, i.e. h\in H^\infty(\Omega)=O(\Omega)\cap L^\infty(\Omega), rather than merely 'h holomorphic'.
The primitive condition should be stated concretely: H\in O(\Omega) with H'=h, equivalently the holomorphic 1-form h(z)\,dz is exact on \Omega.

The converse should be formulated in terms of periods of h(z)\,dz around closed curves in \Omega, i.e. whether the existence of a nontrivial period (equivalently, failure of a single-valued holomorphic primitive) forces a nonzero eigenvalue of S_h.
Because \Omega may be multiply connected, the topological dependence of the question should be made explicit; otherwise the relevance of periods is hidden.
For a stand-alone formulation, the annulus remark should be clearly marked as known evidence rather than part of the question itself.
This paper is a problem list, so there is no numbered conjecture/proposition/theorem to cite here; the target is an unnumbered Scratchpad entry rather than a formal theorem statement.
refined_question: Let \Omega\subset\mathbb C be a smooth bounded planar domain, let T:L^2(\Omega)\to L^2(\Omega) be the canonical L^2-minimal solution operator for \bar\partial on functions (so that for each f\in L^2(\Omega), u=Tf is the unique solution of \bar\partial u=f orthogonal to the Bergman space A^2(\Omega)), and for h\in L^\infty(\Omega) define the compact operator S_h:L^2(\Omega)\to L^2(\Omega) by S_hf=\overline{h}\,Tf. Under what conditions does S_h have a nonzero eigenvalue? In particular, when h\in H^\infty(\Omega) is holomorphic, it is easy to see that if h admits a single-valued holomorphic primitive H\in O(\Omega) on \Omega, then S_h has no nonzero eigenvalues. Is the converse true: if the holomorphic 1-form h(z)\,dz has a nontrivial period on \Omega (equivalently, h has no single-valued holomorphic primitive), must S_h possess a nonzero eigenvalue? For annuli, the answer is yes.
